editorial.headline: The Neighbourhood Shop, Nationally Open but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This is the everyday mixed-goods shop centred on food, drinks or tobacco—open nationally to full foreign ownership, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor, the defining fact is straightforward: this activity cannot be registered through PMA in Bali today. Nationally, it is open to foreign investment with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Bali, however, marks the activity as closed to PMA. The provincial position sits alongside a permanent, island-wide rule blocking all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities for PMA, while the stated Bali rationale reserves minimarkets and supermarkets for Indonesian citizens.

The activity itself belongs to the texture of daily provisioning. It covers retailing a varied mix of necessities principally made up of foodstuffs or prepared food, beverages, and tobacco, conducted outside the self-service model of a minimarket, supermarket, or hypermarket. A shop may also sell selected non-food items—clothing, household furniture, or children’s toys—without changing the essential character of the business. The familiar reference point is a *warung* or a shop for basic household needs: practical, mixed in its stock, and oriented around everyday purchases rather than a self-service retail format.

The national classification does not confine the activity to one business size. It is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That breadth matters because the category describes the nature of the retail operation rather than imposing a single commercial profile. What holds it together is the principal emphasis on food, drinks, or tobacco within a varied-needs retail offer, and the fact that it is not run as a self-service convenience store or larger self-service outlet.

The geographic distinction should therefore be read without smoothing over its consequence. A national PMA opening and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling do not create a Bali registration route where the Bali status is TERTUTUP. For an investor considering Bali, the present answer is not a qualified yes: PMA registration for this activity is closed. For activity planning elsewhere in Indonesia, the national record remains fully foreign-open; in Bali, the provincial restriction is the operative reality.
editorial.pullQuote: A national PMA opening does not create a Bali registration route where Bali marks the activity as closed.
